messages.content:
You are walking along a straight corridor 1.75 m wide. Another person, Person 2, is walking towards you, facing you, 6 m ahead, in the middle of the corridor, as you are. You have decided to move to your left. Tell Person 2 which side of them you will pass on, using their left or right: what do you say?

Answer on the first line with your answer only (a word, a short phrase or a lane number), then give one sentence saying why on the next line.

raw_output:
Their left.

When you move to your left, from Person 2's perspective (facing you), that same side is on their right? Let me check carefully.

You are facing each other. Your left is on the same physical side as Person 2's right, since you are facing opposite directions. So if you move to your left, you will pass on Person 2's right side.

Wait — need to be careful. Corridor width: you move to your left, meaning toward the side of the corridor that is on your left hand. Person 2 is facing you. The side of the corridor on your left is on Person 2's right. So you pass on their right.

But the question asks: "Tell Person 2 which side of them you will pass on, using their left or right." If you move to your left, you pass on their right.

So answer: "Your right."

Let me verify with a concrete setup. Stand facing north. Person 2 is north of you, facing south. Your left is west. You move west. From Person 2's perspective facing south, west is on their right (facing south: left is east, right is west). Yes, west is their right. So you pass on their right.

Answer: Your right.
Reason: Since you are facing each other, the side that is your left is Person 2's right.
